author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Shares of Euronext and Deutsche Boerse rose Monday after Euronext Chief Executive Stéphane Boujnah said he remained open to a combination between the exchanges, Reuters reported. Boujnah said no discussions were currently taking place, leaving the comments as an expression of interest rather than an announced transaction.

At 9:44 a.m. Greenwich Mean Time, Euronext shares were up 2.1% and Deutsche Boerse shares were up 2.9%, according to Reuters. London Stock Exchange Group shares were also higher, gaining 3.8% in the same early-market snapshot.

Any deal would face regulatory and competition questions because the companies operate major trading venues and clearing businesses. For now, the market response reflects renewed speculation, not a merger agreement, formal offer or completed transaction.

Exchange mergers can change where trading and clearing occur, which is why regulators in several jurisdictions would likely review any proposal. The executive’s comments revived the idea without creating a deal for investors to evaluate.
dek: Shares of Euronext and Deutsche Boerse rose after Euronext’s chief executive said he was open to a tie-up, though he said no talks were underway.
headline: Euronext, Deutsche Boerse rise after renewed merger talk
